question: Goldman Sachs Analyst (Software Engineer) Superday / algorithms-and-Java discussion. Questions on Java collections: the **different HashMap types** (for example `HashMap`, `LinkedHashMap`, `TreeMap`, `ConcurrentHashMap`, `Hashtable`), their **internal implementation**, and the **time complexity of their operations**, as part of a wider Java deep dive.
lookingFor: Accurate knowledge of how each map is implemented.
Choosing the right map for a problem.
answer:
**HashMap.** An array of buckets; `index = (n - 1) & hash(key)` (the hash is spread by XOR-ing the high bits). Collisions go into a linked list per bucket; since Java 8 a bucket converts to a **red-black tree** when it holds 8 or more entries and the table has at least 64 buckets. Default capacity 16, load factor 0.75; when `size > capacity * load factor` the table doubles and entries are redistributed. `get`, `put` and `remove` are **O(1) average**, O(log n) worst case with trees (O(n) before Java 8). Allows one null key, not thread-safe, no ordering guarantee. Requires consistent `equals` and `hashCode`.

**LinkedHashMap.** A HashMap plus a doubly linked list threading entries, so iteration follows **insertion order** (or access order with a flag). The same O(1) operations; with `accessOrder=true` and an overridden `removeEldestEntry` it is the standard way to build an **LRU cache**.

**TreeMap.** A **red-black tree** keyed by natural order or a Comparator. `get`, `put`, `remove` are **O(log n)**; sorted iteration, `floorKey`, `ceilingKey`, `subMap`. No null keys (with natural ordering).

**Hashtable.** Legacy; every method is synchronized, no null keys or values; slower than alternatives.

**ConcurrentHashMap.** Thread-safe with high concurrency. Java 7 used segment locks; Java 8+ uses CAS for empty buckets and `synchronized` on the head node of a bucket, with tree bins as well. Reads are lock-free. Operations are O(1) average, no null keys or values, and iterators are weakly consistent. Provides atomic `putIfAbsent`, `compute` and `merge`.

**Others to mention:** `Collections.synchronizedMap` (single lock, wrapper), `IdentityHashMap`, `WeakHashMap`, `EnumMap`.

**Choosing:** HashMap for general use, LinkedHashMap for predictable order or LRU, TreeMap for sorted or range queries, ConcurrentHashMap for shared mutable state across threads.
